subject: Mutual action plan: security checkpoints and retention for PineStreet Bank
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@pinestreetbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan: security checkpoints and retention for PineStreet Bank

Hi Amrita —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our discussion I wanted to lay out the security/compliance checkpoints we expect to include in the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and surface the specific asks you mentioned so we can align the close timeline. High-level: SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ mapping, DPA redline, and clear retention/residency options for logs and backups.

Quick summary of what we can deliver this week:
- SOC 2 Type II report (2025 audit) + one-page control summary
- Completed CAIQ mapping specific to PineStreet (we’ll highlight control gaps if any)
- DPA with our standard redline (I’ve attached the redline draft)
- Proposed retention tiers (30 / 90 / 365 days) and EU residency option for customer data

Ask: can you confirm the acceptance criteria on your side (e.g., SOC 2 + CAIQ OK or do you require live control testing)? Also let me know preferred MAP close window — our proposed timeline below aims for a production POC within 4 weeks of DPA signature.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) Evidence handoff (SOC2 + CAIQ + DPA redline) — Day 0
2) Security Q&A and clarifications — Days 1–5
3) DPA negotiation & signature — Days 6–14
4) POC / limited production (go/no-go) — Days 15–28
5) Final acceptance & onboarding — Day 30

I’m copying Kimberly on operational/legal items. If that schedule looks aggressive for PineStreet we can stretch to an 8-week runway; we want to be flexible.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_redline_v2.pdf (see section on deletion/termination), CAIQ mapping will follow as a workbook.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@pinestreetbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T14:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: security checkpoints and retention for PineStreet Bank

Jonas —

Thanks for the breakdown. A few clarifying questions before we finalize the MAP so Legal & InfoSec can sign off:

1) SOC 2: we require SOC 2 Type II covering the 2025 audit period and prefer a bridge letter if the report is > 6 months old. Will you provide both the report and a short evidence summary (which controls were in-scope)?

2) CAIQ/SIG: please provide the completed CAIQ spreadsheet with control mappings and any compensating controls you rely on. Where there are partial responses, flag them and include remediation timelines.

3) DPA: our legal team has a couple of non-starters — primarily around the deletion language at termination and the backup retention clauses. We need the ability to validate deletion for our controlled data and want a firm maximum backup retention (we typically push 90 days unless exceptions are documented).

4) Residency: we require EU residency for any EU-customer data; for US-resident customer data we accept US-only. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to region-specific tenancy for PSB’s EU customers?

5) Audit logs & retention: what is the default retention window for audit logs, access logs, and KV caches tied to customer sessions? We need that callout in the MAP.

If you can send the SOC2 + CAIQ + your proposed DPA redline, I’ll loop in Liam (legal) and our InfoSec architect to validate.

Best —
Amrita Singh
Head of Security, PineStreet Bank
amrita.singh@pinestreetbank.com

Subject: Fwd: Amrita — security asks (PSB)

Kim / Neha —

FWD from Amrita at PineStreet. Key items: SOC2 + bridge letter, completed CAIQ, DPA deletion/backups, region residency (EU), and explicit retention windows for audit logs & KV cache. I’ve attached the DPA redline we shared in the meeting and our most recent SOC 2 Type II PDF.

Suggested responses we should prepare before sending back to PSB:
- SOC2: provide PDF + one-page control summary and offer a short Q&A call with our auditors if they want live validation. Also provide a bridge statement if necessary.
- CAIQ: deliver completed spreadsheet; flag any partials and give remediation ETA where applicable.
- Retention: propose default audit/log retention = 90 days (configurable to 30/365), backup retention = 365 days, and offer deletion certification upon termination (export + deletion attestation). Note: deletion attestation may require collaboration with infra for snapshot purging timelines; estimate 14–21 days to provide certificate.
- Residency: confirm we can provide region-specific tenancy for EU customers (yes — via Private deploys / region pinning). Need to confirm pricing / lead time if they require 'EU-only' tenancy for production.

We should craft a short "Security Handoff Packet" (SOC2 + CAIQ + DPA redline + evidence links + controls one-pager) and propose a 4-week MAP close with optional 2-week extension.

I’ll draft the outward email for Amrita after we align.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type_ii_2025.pdf; caiaq-pine-street.xlsx; redwood_dpa_redline_v2.pdf

— Jonas

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Amrita — security asks (PSB)

Thanks — a few suggestions before we send to PSB:

1) Package the attachments as a single "Security Handoff Packet" (zip) with a cover page that lists: SOC2 (with audit period), bridge letter policy, CAIQ workbook (with 'red', 'amber', 'green' flag column), and DPA redline summary (call out the deletion & backup clauses).

2) For deletion attestation: propose a 14-day certificate turnaround once we receive the dataset scope and retention targets. Suggest we commit to producing the attestation but reserve limited transition window language (e.g., "reasonable time to purge backups and snapshots, not to exceed 21 days") to avoid unrealistic contractual expectations.

3) Retention options: offer default 90 days for audit/logs, optional 30-day (for higher privacy customers) or 365-day (for longer-term analytics) with pricing/ops caveat. Make sure to call out KV cache expiry is functionally 24–72 hours by default unless customers request caching policies (we can persist or flush per contract).

4) Residency: confirm we can do EU-only tenancy for their EU customers via Redwood Private / Dedicated. Note this may require a short lead time (2–4 weeks) and additional onboarding steps (networking/KMS). Capture this as an "ops dependency" in the MAP.

5) MAP timeline: I prefer a 6-week runway by default given legal negotiations. Proposed detailed cadence:
 - Week 0: Security Handoff Packet delivered
 - Week 1: PSB asks & clarifications
 - Week 2: DPA negotiation (redlines back-and-forth)
 - Week 3–4: POC (data residency config + smoke tests)
 - Week 5: Final remediation & acceptance testing
 - Week 6: Go-live / onboarding

If PSB pushes for faster close we can keep the structure but mark the DPA negotiation as the primary risk. I can draft the cover page + suggested DPA language around deletion/backup and share for review.

I’ll attach the cover page + packet once done (security-handoff-packet.zip).

—Kimberly
Legal & Ops Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@pinestreetbank.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@pinestreetbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-31T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: security checkpoints and retention for PineStreet Bank

Amrita / Liam —

Following up with the materials and a proposed MAP timeline. Per Amrita’s asks, attached is the Security Handoff Packet (SOC2 Type II PDF, CAIQ workbook, and our DPA redline).

- SOC2: redwood_soc2_type_ii_2025.pdf included + one-page control summary in the packet. If you need a bridge letter we can issue one (our audits are annual; bridge letters are available on request).

- CAIQ: caiaq-pine-street.xlsx is completed and contains a column called "PSB Notes" where we flagged partials and remediation ETAs.

- DPA & deletion: redwood_dpa_redline_v2.pdf highlights the deletion and backup sections. Our proposed wording: "Redwood will provide export of customer-scoped data upon termination and certify deletion of live datasets within 14 days, with backup snapshot purging to be completed within a maximum of 21 days; Redwood will provide a deletion attestation once purge is complete." We’re happy to adjust language but request a short transitional window for infra operations.

- Retention & KV cache: default audit/log retention = 90 days (configurable to 30 or 365). KV cache (session-level) expiry default is 48 hours; persistent caching for analytics is available under a separate configuration and will be explicitly listed in the MAP if requested.

- Residency: we can provide EU-only tenancy for EU-custodied datasets via Redwood Private / Dedicated deployments. Ops lead time is ~2–4 weeks depending on network/KMS setup; we’ll include the deployment lead time as a MAP dependency.

Proposed MAP timeline (we can compress if necessary):
- Day 0: Security Handoff Packet delivered (today)
- Days 1–5: Q&A & clarifications
- Days 6–20: DPA negotiation & signature (aim for signature by Day 14, flexible)
- Days 21–35: POC (residency config + smoke tests)
- Day 36: Final acceptance

Next steps: please confirm whether SOC2 + CAIQ + the DPA redline are sufficient for InfoSec to start internal review and whether the proposed deletion attestation timing is acceptable. If you want us to tighten the deletion language we can escalate to legal but that may add to negotiation time.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.com/deals/PSB-4829), DPA draft via DocuSign (https://docusign.com/PSB-DPA-v2).

Thanks for the quick responses — we’re ready to move forward once you confirm acceptance criteria and timing.

Best —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: security-handoff-packet.zip (SOC2, CAIQ workbook, DPA redline summary)
